title: The X-ray-to-UV relation does not evolve in homogeneous quasar samples
comment: 10 Pages, 8 Figures. Submitted to A&A. Comments welcome
summary:
We present a new, highly homogeneous quasar sample with X-ray and UV observations optimized to reliably estimate distances via the non-linear X-ray-to-UV relation. Cross-matching the Sloan Digital Sky Survey DR16 quasar catalog with the XMM-Newton serendipitous catalogue (4XMM--DR14), we employ strict selection criteria to build a robust sample: (1) UV and (2) X-ray colour constraints to avoid, respectively, extinction and absorption; (3) removal of broad absorption line and radio-bright quasars; (4) exclusion of sources at z<0.7 to prevent galactic UV contamination; and (5) rejection of sources with shallow X-ray observations. The latter step, closely related to the Eddington bias, is critical because SDSS data are generally deeper than X-ray data for typical quasar spectral energy distributions: ignoring such a discrepancy introduces a spurious redshift dependence in the X-ray-to-UV relation parameters. Our final sample contains about 2,000 quasars at z=0.7--5. We demonstrate that the X-ray-to-UV relation is constant across this redshift range, with a mean slope of 0.58\,$\pm$\,0.01 and a dispersion of 0.15 dex.
  Our findings confirm the intrinsic stability of this relation over cosmic time, emphasizing that both homogeneity and robust Eddington bias corrections are vital for flux-limited samples.
  In fact, the impact of the preferential detection of X-ray brighter-than-average sources near the effective sensitivity limits significantly grows with redshift. Any resulting evolutionary trend in the X-ray-to-UV relation, especially in the form a slope flattening, is therefore either a largely spurious effect, or the result of mixing populations of quasars with intrinsically different spectral properties.

AI.tldr: A robust quasar sample with careful bias correction confirms the intrinsic stability of the X-ray-to-UV relation across redshift 0.7 to 5, debunking spurious evolution claims driven by data selection effects and spectral property mixing.
AI.motivation: To develop a highly homogeneous quasar sample with reliable distance estimations using the non-linear X-ray-to-UV relation, addressing issues such as bias and data heterogeneity that affect previous studies.
AI.method: Cross-matching the SDSS DR16 quasar catalog with the XMM-Newton 4XMM-DR14 catalog under strict selection criteria (UV and X-ray colour constraints, exclusion of broad absorption line and radio-bright quasars, redshift cut-off, and rejection of shallow X-ray observations) to build a robust and unbiased sample optimized for studying the X-ray-to-UV relation.
AI.result: The final sample contains ~2,000 quasars between z=0.7-5; the X-ray-to-UV relation is confirmed to be constant across this range with a mean slope of 0.58 ± 0.01 and a dispersion of 0.15 dex, demonstrating intrinsic stability over cosmic time, highlighting importance of correcting Eddington bias and ensuring homogeneity for flux-limited samples.
AI.conclusion: The observed evolutionary trends in the X-ray-to-UV relation, such as slope flattening with redshift, are either spurious due to selection biases like the Eddington bias or caused by mixing quasar populations with different intrinsic spectral properties. Correcting these biases is essential to preserve the intrinsic stability of the relation.

title: The Effects of Cosmic Ray Protons on Galactic Nonthermal Filaments
comment: Submitted to ApJ, 17 pages, 11 figures, comments welcome
summary: The Galactic Center (GC) contains a collection of filaments that are typically tens of parsecs in length, illuminated by synchrotron radiation from cosmic rays (CR). The origin of these nonthermal filaments (NTFs) is unclear. We aim to distinguish two injection mechanisms: the first mechanism posits that NTFs are fueled either by jets from pulsar wind nebulae and are lepton-dominated; the second mechanism posits that NTFs are fueled by accelerated particles from interstellar shocks and are proton-dominated. We explore these mechanisms using the magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code Athena++, modified to account for radiative and collisional losses, to simulate CR propagation with lepton and proton CR species. We vary parameters such as magnetic field strength, plasma density, and the CR diffusion coefficient to determine how the range of conditions present in the GC can affect CRs' propagation, heating, plasma flow, and the observed synchrotron emission. We find few observable differences between the proton- and lepton-dominated cases, but comparing the models with observed filament properties motivates consideration of a third formation mechanism: the generation of NTFs arise from intermittent structures in Galactic Center turbulence.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the origins of Galactic Center nonthermal filaments using MHD simulations of cosmic ray propagation, finding minimal observational differences between proton- and lepton-fueled models and proposing that turbulent structures may better explain the filaments' formation.
AI.motivation: The origin of nonthermal filaments (NTFs) in the Galactic Center (GC) is unclear, with competing theories about their particle injection mechanisms.
AI.method: The study uses the magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code Athena++ with modifications to include radiative and collisional losses, simulating cosmic ray (CR) propagation with both leptons and protons under varying GC physical parameters.
AI.result: The simulations reveal few observable differences between proton- and lepton-dominated injection cases. However, comparison with observed filament properties suggests that a third mechanism, involving turbulence-induced intermittent structures, may be responsible for NTF formation.
AI.conclusion: Neither the proton-dominated nor the lepton-dominated injection mechanisms alone fully explain the NTFs' properties in the GC, indicating that turbulence-driven intermittent structures could contribute significantly to their formation.

title: Isolated neutron star candidates from the fourth generation XMM-Newton catalogues
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, A&A accepted
summary: X-ray thermally emitting isolated neutron stars (XINSs) are a rare population that provides insights into neutron star cooling, magnetic-field evolution, and Galactic demographics. Using more than two decades of observations from the European Space Agency's XMM-Newton Observatory, we searched the 4XMM-DR9 and 4XMM-DR12 catalogues for absorbed XINS candidates down to a flux of $10^{-14}$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ in the 0.5--1 keV band. Candidates were selected based on soft X-ray spectra and the absence of catalogued optical, ultraviolet, or infrared counterparts. Follow-up observations with XMM-Newton and FAST were complemented by data from the SRG/eROSITA All-Sky Survey, Chandra, and optical surveys. Of ten sources analysed, five are compelling XINS candidates, one is the known XINS 4XMM J022141.5-735632, two are extragalactic contaminants, and two remain ambiguous because of limited photon statistics. The five candidates exhibit soft ($kT\sim80-100$ eV), moderately absorbed, and stable X-ray emission consistent with distant XINSs. They are located primarily in the Galactic plane, with possible associations at distances of $\sim$1.8 and $\sim$6 kpc. Population-synthesis simulations predict $20\pm5$ XINSs within the 4XMM-DR12 footprint, of which $6^{+2}_{-3}$ exceed our flux threshold, consistent with the observed sample if additional candidates are confirmed. The model further predicts that $\sim$70% of the population remains below the detection threshold. Deep optical and additional X-ray observations are required to establish the nature of the candidates. Future missions such as NewAthena will enable more detailed studies of these distant populations and improve constraints on the Galactic XINS population.

AI.tldr: Using 20+ years of XMM-Newton data and complementary observations, researchers identified five new isolated neutron star candidates based on soft X-ray emission, consistent with models predicting many undetected XINSs. Further observations are needed, with future missions promising enhanced insights.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize the rare population of X-ray thermally emitting isolated neutron stars (XINSs) to gain insights into neutron star cooling, magnetic-field evolution, and Galactic demographics.
AI.method: A systematic search of absorbed XINS candidates was conducted using over two decades of data from the XMM-Newton Observatory's 4XMM-DR9 and 4XMM-DR12 catalogues, focusing on soft X-ray spectra and absence of optical, UV, or IR counterparts; complemented by follow-up observations from XMM-Newton, FAST, SRG/eROSITA, Chandra, and optical surveys; candidates were analyzed for spectral properties and location.
AI.result: Ten sources were analyzed, identifying five compelling new XINS candidates exhibiting soft, moderately absorbed, stable X-ray emissions consistent with distant XINSs, one known XINS, two extragalactic contaminants, and two ambiguous cases. Population synthesis agrees with the observed numbers within flux thresholds and predicts a larger undetected XINS population (~70%).
AI.conclusion: The study expands the known population of XINS candidates, aligns observations with population synthesis predictions, and highlights the need for deeper optical and X-ray follow-up to confirm candidate nature. Upcoming missions like NewAthena will improve understanding of the Galactic XINS population.

title: Population synthesis of Galactic middle-aged pulsar wind nebulae II. Observational signatures of superefficiency
comment: 16 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables; submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: Pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) interacting with the host supernova remnants (SNRs) can enter the reverberation phase in which reverse-shock-driven compression amplifies the magnetic field and rapidly reprocesses particles, sometimes producing "superefficiency", where the radiative output in a given frequency band exceeds the pulsar's instantaneous spin-down power. We investigate the prevalence of this phenomenon in the Galactic population by modeling PWNe with the hybrid TIDE+L framework, which self-consistently follows dynamical evolution, particle spectra, and emission from radio to PeV energies. We track superefficiency across frequency bands and evolutionary stages, analyzing both individual objects and ensemble properties, including compression-resolved samples and population spectral energy distributions. Superefficiency is most common in the far-infrared, but emerges across frequencies and evolutionary phases. It is enhanced in systems where accumulated low-energy electrons radiate in magnetically amplified nebulae. We predict substantially more superefficient sources than a purely thin-shell model would, with differences ranging from factors of a few in FIR and GeV bands to more than an order of magnitude in several optical/UV/X-ray bands.

AI.tldr: This paper models pulsar wind nebulae interacting with supernova remnants to show that magnetic compression during reverberation phases frequently causes superefficiency—where emission exceeds pulsar spin-down power—especially in far-infrared and other bands, with more such sources predicted than previous models suggested.
AI.motivation: To investigate how common the superefficiency phenomenon is in Galactic pulsar wind nebulae interacting with supernova remnants during the reverberation phase.
AI.method: Modeling PWNe using the hybrid TIDE+L framework that self-consistently follows dynamical evolution, particle spectra, and multi-wavelength emission from radio to PeV energies, tracking superefficiency across frequency bands and evolutionary stages for both individual and population samples.
AI.result: Superefficiency is most frequently observed in the far-infrared but occurs across various frequencies and stages, particularly enhanced in magnetically amplified nebulae with accumulated low-energy electrons. The study predicts substantially more superefficient sources compared to thin-shell models, with differences ranging from several times up to over an order of magnitude depending on frequency band.
AI.conclusion: Superefficiency in PWNe during reverberation is a widespread phenomenon across multiple frequency bands and evolutionary stages, influenced significantly by magnetic field amplification and electron accumulation, suggesting that realistic dynamic modeling predicts a much higher occurrence rate than simpler models.

title: CMBolic: Symbolic emulators for the Cosmic Microwave Background. I. Lensing
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures. Code available at https://github.com/dvokrouhlicky/CMBolic
summary: We present the first installment of CMBolic: a suite of symbolic cosmic microwave background (CMB) emulators. In this instance, we emulate the CMB lensing potential power spectrum $C_\ell^{φφ}$ for the widely used extended $Λ$CDM model which simultaneously includes massive neutrinos and evolving dark energy modelled using the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parameterization. We achieve comparable precision to existing neural network emulators, with the added benefit of simpler handling as our emulators are analytic functions of the model parameters and multipole $\ell$. On independent validation spectra evaluated in the range $2\leq \ell \leq 5500$, CMBolic achieves mean absolute fractional errors of $0.27\%$ in the $Λ$CDM subspace and $0.32\%$ across the full extended parameter space. This emulation error is well below even the most optimistic noise forecasts from CMB Stage 4 experiments. We apply CMBolic to cosmological parameter estimation with Bayesian inference using the lensing-only likelihoods from ACT DR6 and Planck. We show excellent agreement between the posteriors obtained by CMBolic and the Boltzmann code CLASS. This demonstrates the practical use of CMBolic on cosmological parameter estimation, reducing the runtime from 2 weeks to under 3 minutes.

AI.tldr: CMBolic is a symbolic emulator suite for CMB lensing power spectra of extended $\Lambda$CDM models, achieving high precision with analytic functions and drastically speeding up cosmological parameter estimation while maintaining agreement with standard Boltzmann codes.
AI.motivation: To develop efficient and accurate symbolic emulators for the CMB lensing potential power spectrum that handle extended cosmological models including massive neutrinos and evolving dark energy, improving upon existing neural network methods in simplicity and speed.
AI.method: Constructing analytic symbolic emulators (CMBolic) for the CMB lensing potential power spectrum $C_\ell^{φφ}$ over the extended $\Lambda$CDM parameter space including CPL parameterization for dark energy, validating precision against Boltzmann code CLASS, and applying Bayesian parameter estimation with real lensing data.
AI.result: CMBolic achieves mean absolute fractional errors of 0.27% within $\Lambda$CDM and 0.32% across the full extended space, outperforming noise thresholds for future experiments; it produces posteriors matching CLASS results while reducing parameter estimation runtime drastically from two weeks to under 3 minutes.
AI.conclusion: Symbolic emulators like CMBolic provide a precise, fast, and easily handled alternative to neural network emulators for extended $\Lambda$CDM cosmological models, enabling efficient cosmological parameter estimation with real data without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Old pulsar wind nebulae and the role of the thermal filaments
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Old pulsar wind nebulae are among the foremost galactic high-energy gamma-ray sources. However we still lack a robust approach to their modeling, especially in the light of forthcoming high-energy observatories like Astri or CTAO. Part of the problem is due to the complex interaction that characterizes these systems. Understanding this complexity has then become mandatory for further advancements. We aim to develop a new approach to investigate the role the thermal thick layer of massive filaments, seen in objects like the Crab nebula and 3C 58, but likely present in all pulsar wind nebulae, can exert on the dynamics of the late reverberation phase, and compare results with standard approaches that neglect such a layer. A new formulation of the one-zone thin-shell plus Lagrangian formalism, developed in a series of previous papers, is here extended to the case of a thick layer of filamentary ejecta, complementing our former work, mostly focused on the initial free-expansion phase. We compare the dynamics of reverberation with and without the presence of filaments, and show that in the former case reverberation may be substantially anticipated and the following compression takes much longer. The total compression of the system does not seem to change much, and the qualitative behavior is preserved. Our results suggest that the presence or absence of an extended filamentary layer might affect the duration of both the free-expansion phase (shortening it) and the following compression phase during reverberation (lengthening it), but it does not change much the overall compression of the nebula. While this changes the relative number of systems in these two phases, and their contribution to high-energy emission, some peculiar radiative effects associated with the level of compression in old systems, like the "super-efficiency", might not be much affected.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new modeling approach accounting for thick filamentary layers in old pulsar wind nebulae, showing it shifts the timing of expansion and compression phases during reverberation but leaves total compression and key radiative behaviors mostly unaffected.
AI.motivation: Current models for old pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) are insufficient, particularly as new high-energy observatories are coming online, due to the complex physical interactions involved.
AI.method: Development and extension of a one-zone thin-shell plus Lagrangian formalism to include a thick layer of massive filamentary ejecta, allowing for comparison of reverberation dynamics with and without such filaments.
AI.result: Inclusion of the filamentary layer anticipates the reverberation phase and prolongs the subsequent compression phase, although total compression and qualitative behavior remain largely unchanged.
AI.conclusion: The presence of a thick filamentary layer alters the timing and duration of phases in PWN evolution, impacting their high-energy emission characteristics, but does not significantly affect overall nebula compression or certain radiative effects like super-efficiency.

title: Measurements of the Angular Homogeneity Scale from DESI DR1
comment: 24 pages, 24 figures, 3 tables, 4 appendix
summary:
The study of the large-scale distribution of galaxies provides essential information for testing the standard cosmological model, namely the $Λ$CDM paradigm. This scenario is based upon two foundations: General Relativity as the theory of gravity, and the Cosmological Principle, which states that the Universe is statistically homogeneous and isotropic on large scales -- so that we can measure distances and ages in the Universe assuming the FLRW metric.
  In this work, we perform a test of the Cosmological Principle by probing the angular homogeneity scale, $θ_H$, using the state-of-the-art observational data of Luminous Red Galaxies (LRGs) from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI DR1). Our analysis is performed exclusively in two dimensions, across narrow redshift ranges inside a larger redshift sample of $0.4 < z < 1.1$, in two different surveyed regions of the sky (North and South Galactic Caps), as we want to minimize a priori dependences on an underlying cosmological model.
  We obtain that such a scale is indeed identified in all redshift ranges, and that they are consistent with mock simulations assuming the $Λ$CDM model. Moreover, our results are in great agreement with previous measurements using Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey Data Release 16 (SDSS-IV eBOSS DR16), as well as between the north and south galactic caps of the DESI DR1 survey. These findings help underpinning statistical isotropy and homogeneity of the Universe as a physically valid hypothesis in light of upcoming stage-IV redshift surveys, hence are consistent with one of the fundamental pillars of the standard cosmological model.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the Cosmological Principle by measuring the angular homogeneity scale using DESI DR1 Luminous Red Galaxy data, finding results consistent with the $Λ$CDM model and previous surveys, thereby reinforcing the Universe's large-scale statistical isotropy and homogeneity.
AI.motivation: To test the validity of the Cosmological Principle, which underlies the standard $Λ$CDM cosmological model, by investigating the angular homogeneity scale of the Universe.
AI.method: Analysis of the angular homogeneity scale $θ_H$ using 2D data of Luminous Red Galaxies from DESI DR1, across narrow redshift bins from $0.4 < z < 1.1$, in two sky regions (North and South Galactic Caps), minimizing model dependence.
AI.result: Identification of the angular homogeneity scale in all redshift ranges, consistent with $Λ$CDM-based mock simulations and previous measurements from SDSS-IV eBOSS DR16, with agreement between North and South Galactic Caps.
AI.conclusion: The Universe is statistically homogeneous and isotropic on large scales, supporting the Cosmological Principle as a valid assumption of the standard cosmological model based on current and forthcoming galaxy survey data.

title: Faraday Complexity and Depolarisation in a High-Rotation-Measure Radio Galaxy from the Spectra and Polarisation In Cutouts of Extragalactic Sources (SPICE-RACS) DR2
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables, submitted
summary: We present a broadband spectro-polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic radio source \texttt{RACS\_0900-28\_7036} using SPICE-RACS DR2 observations with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). The source was selected for its large rotation measure (${\rm RM}=345.7\pm0.2~{\rm rad~m^{-2}}$), substantial excess relative to the local foreground ($Δ{\rm RM}\approx171~{\rm rad~m^{-2}}$), and strong evidence of Faraday complexity ($σ_{\rm add}/δσ_{\rm add}\approx8.6$). Observations span 803--1083~MHz in 36 spectral channels, enabling detailed characterization of Faraday rotation and wavelength-dependent depolarization. One-dimensional $q$-$u$ fitting and Bayesian model selection identify a multi-component model comprising one Burn-slab component and two external Faraday dispersion components (1 Slab + 2 EFD) as the preferred description. The dominant astrophysical component exhibits ${\rm RM}\approx345.5~{\rm rad~m^{-2}}$ with modest Faraday dispersion ($σ_{\rm RM}\approx3~{\rm rad~m^{-2}}$), while a secondary broader component at ${\rm RM}\approx131.5~{\rm rad~m^{-2}}$ shows strong depolarization ($σ_{\rm RM}\approx19.5~{\rm rad~m^{-2}}$). The fractional polarization spectrum and $q$--$u$ plane evolution further confirm multiple Faraday-active regions along the line of sight. These results demonstrate that ASKAP broadband spectropolarimetry can resolve complex Faraday structures and probe turbulent magnetized environments, providing a framework for systematic depolarization studies across the full SPICE-RACS catalog and enabling statistical investigations of Faraday complexity in diverse extragalactic radio sources.

AI.tldr: Using ASKAP broadband spectropolarimetry, this study reveals complex Faraday rotation and depolarization structures in an extragalactic radio source, demonstrating the capability to characterize multiple Faraday-active components and turbulence in magnetized environments.
AI.motivation: To investigate complex Faraday rotation and depolarization structures in extragalactic radio sources using broadband spectro-polarimetric data.
AI.method: Broadband spectro-polarimetric analysis using ASKAP SPICE-RACS DR2 data across 803–1083 MHz with 36 spectral channels, applying one-dimensional q-u fitting and Bayesian model selection to identify Faraday-active components.
AI.result: Identified a multi-component Faraday model (1 Burn-slab + 2 external Faraday dispersion components) with distinct rotation measures and depolarization characteristics, confirming multiple Faraday-active regions along the line of sight and resolving complex Faraday structures.
AI.conclusion: ASKAP broadband spectropolarimetry effectively resolves complex Faraday rotation and depolarization, enabling detailed studies of turbulent magnetized environments and facilitating systematic depolarization analysis across large radio source catalogs.

title: Discovery of a Candidate 2 keV Cyclotron Resonance Scattering Feature in the HLX NGC 3583 X-1
comment: 20 pages, 9 figures. Revised version submitted to The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We present a broadband X-ray study of the transient hyperluminous X-ray source (HLX), 2SXPS J111416.1+481833, in the galaxy NGC 3583, using archival XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, Chandra data, and long-term Swift/XRT monitoring. The source episodically enters the hyperluminous regime with X-ray luminosities $L_X > 10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and drops by a factor of $>45$ from its peak into a deep low state. We detect a clear spectral cutoff at $\sim$5-6 keV in the broadband spectra, which are well modeled by a soft thermal component combined with optically thick thermal Comptonization or an inner advection-dominated disk. In the XMM-Newton spectra, we detect a statistically significant ($\gtrsim 3.9 σ$) absorption line centered at $E_{\rm line} \approx 1.97 \pm 0.04$ keV with a width of $σ_{\rm line} \approx 74 \pm 40$ eV. We primarily interpret the line as a candidate proton Cyclotron Resonance Scattering Feature (CRSF), implying a local magnetic field strength of $B \sim 4 \times 10^{14}$ G. Alternative interpretations, such as an origin in an ionized outflow, were explored and found to be less likely. We do not detect coherent X-ray pulsations, placing 90% confidence upper limits on the pulsed fraction of 19.3% in the 0.3-10 keV band and 36.3% in the 3-15 keV band. The combination of extreme luminosity, a hard spectral state, and the detection of a candidate cyclotron line provides strong evidence for a highly magnetized neutron star accretor.

AI.tldr: A detailed X-ray study of the hyperluminous X-ray source 2SXPS J111416.1+481833 reveals episodic extreme luminosity, a spectral cutoff around 5-6 keV, and a candidate proton cyclotron absorption line indicating a strong magnetic field (~4x10^14 G), supporting a highly magnetized neutron star accretor without detected pulsations.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature and accretion mechanisms of the transient hyperluminous X-ray source 2SXPS J111416.1+481833 in galaxy NGC 3583 by characterizing its spectral and temporal properties across multiple X-ray observations.
AI.method: Broadband X-ray data analysis was performed using archival observations from XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, Chandra, and long-term monitoring by Swift/XRT. Spectral fitting included models with soft thermal components combined with optically thick thermal Comptonization or advection-dominated disk models, and statistical tests were applied to identify spectral features such as absorption lines. Pulsation searches were conducted to constrain pulsed fractions.
AI.result: The source shows episodic hyperluminous states with luminosities exceeding 10^41 erg s^-1 and can decrease in intensity by over a factor of 45. A significant spectral cutoff around 5-6 keV was detected, and a statistically significant absorption line near 1.97 keV was found, interpreted primarily as a proton Cyclotron Resonance Scattering Feature indicating a magnetic field of ~4x10^14 G. No coherent X-ray pulsations were detected within upper limits of the pulsed fraction. These findings strongly suggest the accretor is a highly magnetized neutron star.
AI.conclusion: The observed extreme luminosity, spectral cutoff, and candidate proton cyclotron absorption line provide compelling evidence that the source 2SXPS J111416.1+481833 is powered by accretion onto a highly magnetized neutron star rather than alternative compact objects or emission mechanisms.

title: Effective Bayesian ranking of low order monomial potentials in low temperature warm inflation
comment: 34 pages, 4 figures
summary: An effective Bayesian evidence ranking is performed for the monomial potentials \(V_p(φ)=λ_pφ^p/p\), with \(p=2,3,4\), in low temperature warm inflation with the dissipative coefficient fixed as \(Υ=C_φT^3/φ^2\). In cold single field slow roll inflation, these branches are strongly constrained by the observational upper bound on the tensor to scalar ratio \(r=\mathcal P_T/\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}\), whereas warm inflation can reduce this tension by enhancing the scalar spectrum. The relevant question is therefore which monomial power is favored once \(A_s\), \(n_s\), \(r_{0.05}\), and the viable parameter volume are considered simultaneously. For each branch, the warm background equations including radiation backreaction are solved, and a broadened compressed likelihood for \((A_s,n_s,r_{0.05})\) is integrated over the prior volume to obtain \(Z_{\rm eff}^{(A_s,n_s,r)}\). For \(N_*=55\), \(σ_r=0.005\), and structure conditioned priors covering viable warm branches, the quadratic and cubic potentials are disfavored relative to the quartic branch: $Δ\ln Z_{\rm eff}(p=2)=-32.18,~ Δ\ln Z_{\rm eff}(p=3)=-6.99.$ This hierarchy is stable under changes in \(N_*\), prior ranges, random seeds, and the $r$ bound treatment. A representative quartic trajectory gives \(n_s=0.96420\), \(r_{0.05}=0.02663\), \(Q_*=4.68\times10^{-3}\), and \(T_*/H_*=10.67\), corresponding to a weakly dissipative but thermally occupied CMB window. Decomposing the primordial spectrum shows that the quartic preference is driven mainly by Bose Einstein occupation enhancement for \(T_*/H_*>1\), not by strong dissipative friction. Within the low temperature dissipative effective class and compressed likelihood adopted here, the evidence hierarchy is \(p=4>p=3\gg p=2.\)

AI.tldr: Bayesian analysis of monomial warm inflation potentials shows quartic power strongly favored over quadratic and cubic, mainly due to thermal effects enhancing scalar perturbations, resolving cold inflation tensions.
AI.motivation: To resolve tension in cold inflation constraints by assessing which monomial potential power is favored in low temperature warm inflation given observational data.
AI.method: Bayesian evidence ranking integrating broadened likelihood over prior parameter volume while solving warm inflation background equations with radiation backreaction, focusing on monomial potentials with fixed dissipative coefficient.
AI.result: Quartic potential (p=4) is strongly favored over quadratic (p=2) and cubic (p=3) branches, stable under various parameter changes; preference driven by Bose-Einstein enhancement, not strong dissipation.
AI.conclusion: Within the studied framework, the quartic monomial potential is the most viable warm inflation candidate, significantly outperforming quadratic and cubic potentials in explaining observational data.

title: XRISM Observations of Abell 1795: Evidence for Low Turbulence and Resonant Scattering
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: We present high-resolution X-ray spectroscopic observations of the cool-core galaxy cluster Abell~1795 obtained with XRISM/Resolve. The cluster was observed with two deep pointings: a 225 ks central exposure and a 113 ks northern exposure, extending to a projected radius of 320 kpc from the cluster center. Single-temperature fits reveal a clear radial gradient in the line-of-sight velocity dispersion, decreasing from 114 $\pm$ 11 km/s in the core to 68 $\pm$ 39 km/s at 320 kpc. The bulk velocities in the central regions are very low (22 $\pm$ 12 and 7 $\pm$ 21 km/s), indicating no significant relative motion between the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) and the intracluster medium (ICM). Given that the central region includes the southward extending cool gas tail, this result disfavors the ``cooling-wake'' scenario and instead supports an AGN-uplift origin. We find that the nonthermal pressure fraction decreases with radius, from $P_{\rm NT}/P_{\rm T}\approx2\%$ in the core to $\sim0.6\%$ at 330 kpc, suggesting that the northern ICM of A1795 is largely quiescent. Two-temperature and split energy-band (2--4 keV and 6--7 keV) fits identify two gas phases within the central $<1.5'$ region, providing strong evidence for multiphase gas in the cluster core. We detect a $\sim14\%$ resonant suppression of the optically thick Fe XXV $w$ line in the center. Additionally, we observe a significant excess in the Fe XXV $y$ line-flux relative to models. Accounting for uncertainties in the atomic data reduces this discrepancy, suggesting that atomic data uncertainties may contribute to the observed residual flux.

AI.tldr: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of Abell 1795 reveals low central bulk velocities, a radial decrease in velocity dispersion and nonthermal pressure, strong evidence for multiphase gas in the core, and subtle line flux anomalies likely influenced by atomic data uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To investigate the gas dynamics and multiphase structure in the cool-core galaxy cluster Abell 1795 using high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy.
AI.method: Performed deep X-ray spectroscopic observations of Abell 1795 with XRISM/Resolve, using single-temperature, two-temperature, and split energy-band spectral fitting analyses.
AI.result: Revealed a radial gradient in velocity dispersion with low central bulk velocities, indicating no significant motion between BCG and ICM; found nonthermal pressure decreases with radius suggesting a quiescent ICM; detected multiphase gas in the core and resonant suppression as well as excess flux in specific Fe XXV lines, partly explained by atomic data uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: The results disfavor the cooling-wake scenario for the cool gas tail and support an AGN-driven uplift origin; the northern ICM is largely quiescent with multiphase gas present in the core, and atomic data uncertainties impact the interpretation of Fe line fluxes.

title: On The Nature of Einstein Probe Transient EP250916a: Insights from X-ray, Optical, and Radio Observations
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal, 16 pages, 7 figures
summary: We report multi-wavelength studies of the transient EP250916a, detected by the Einstein Probe on 2025 September 16. Located at low Galactic latitude, the source exhibited a rapid X-ray brightening, reaching an unabsorbed 0.5--10 keV flux of $(6.4 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-10}$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, followed by a plateau and a two-stage decay lasting over 40 days. Swift/XRT monitoring shows a persistently hard spectrum ($Γ\approx 1.6$--2.2) with only modest softening during decay, while a NuSTAR observation confirms a hard-state continuum extending up to 70 keV. Timing analysis of XMM-Newton data reveals a weak quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) at $\sim$13 Hz. No other coherent pulsations or thermonuclear bursts are detected. Broadband spectral modeling favors a nonthermal power-law continuum with partial-covering absorption, and shows no significant thermal disk component. Optical imaging obtained with NOT/ALFOSC, LCO, and GaiaDR3 identifies two faint sources within the 2 arcsec Swift/XRT positional uncertainty. A MeerKAT observation at 1.28 GHz yielded no radio counterpart, with a 3$σ$ upper limit of 60 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$. The combination of a long-lasting outburst, a hard nonthermal X-ray spectrum, a weak QPO detection, the absence of coherent timing features, and faint potential optical counterparts disfavors a stellar-flare or extragalactic origin and supports an accreting compact-object scenario. Comparisons with similar faint, hard-state transients place EP250916a within a growing population of low-luminosity, hard-state black hole X-ray binary candidates.

AI.tldr: Multi-wavelength observations of transient EP250916a reveal characteristics of a low-luminosity, hard-state black hole X-ray binary, including a hard X-ray spectrum, weak QPO, and lack of thermal or pulsation features, ruling out stellar flares or extragalactic origins.
AI.motivation: To characterize and understand the nature of the transient EP250916a detected by the Einstein Probe, by analyzing its multi-wavelength observations and spectral features to ascertain its astrophysical origin.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength monitoring including X-ray observations by Einstein Probe, Swift/XRT, NuSTAR, and XMM-Newton, optical imaging with NOT/ALFOSC, LCO, GaiaDR3, and radio observations with MeerKAT; spectral modeling and timing analysis including QPO detection and broadband spectral fitting were conducted.
AI.result: The transient showed a rapid X-ray brightening followed by a plateau and two-stage decay with a persistently hard X-ray spectrum extending up to 70 keV, a weak 13 Hz QPO, and no thermal disk component or coherent pulsations; optical counterparts are faint and no radio detection was made. These properties suggest an accreting compact object, likely a low-luminosity, hard-state black hole X-ray binary candidate.
AI.conclusion: EP250916a is unlikely to be a stellar flare or extragalactic source and is best explained as a new member of low-luminosity, hard-state black hole X-ray binaries, characterized by its long-lasting outburst, hard nonthermal spectrum, weak QPO, and faint optical counterparts.

title: Reconciling large-scale Lyman-$α$ correlations with the SCRIPT Semi-numerical Model
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures. To be submitted to JCAP
summary: Recent analyses of high-redshift Lyman-$α$ forest observations have revealed strong correlations on scales exceeding 200 cMpc at redshift z = 6. Reproducing these large-scale correlations has proven challenging for current large-volume reionization simulations. In this work, we investigate these large-scale correlations using mock spectra generated from the extended SCRIPT semi-numerical reionization model. We find that while the fiducial model ensemble systematically predicts smaller correlation lengths than those inferred from the 67 sightlines in the extended XQR-30 sample, a small fraction of individual mock realizations can naturally reproduce the observed signal. Using a delete-2 jackknife analysis, we demonstrate that the observed large-scale correlation length is disproportionately driven by a rare pair of highly transmissive sightlines associated with high-redshift transmission spikes. By inserting two such highly transmissive sightlines into our mock realizations, the fraction of models consistent with the observed redshift evolution and correlation length increases significantly from 17.5% to 74.1%. Furthermore, we show that spatial fluctuations in the ionizing mean free path remain an essential physical ingredient for reproducing the observed correlation structure. Our results suggest that the unexpectedly large Lyman-$α$ correlations can be reconciled with existing reionization models when accounting for cosmic variance and the outsized statistical impact of rare, highly transmissive sightlines.

AI.tldr: This study explains unexpectedly large Lyman-α forest correlations at redshift 6 by showing they arise from rare, highly transmissive sightlines and cosmic variance, reconciling observations with current reionization models using a semi-numerical approach.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of unexpectedly large-scale correlations in high-redshift Lyman-α forest observations, which have proven difficult to reproduce with current large-volume reionization simulations.
AI.method: Use of mock spectra generated from the extended SCRIPT semi-numerical reionization model, coupled with delete-2 jackknife analysis and insertion of highly transmissive sightlines into mock realizations to study the correlation length and its drivers.
AI.result: A small fraction of mock realizations can reproduce the observed large-scale correlations. The large-scale correlation length is driven disproportionately by rare, highly transmissive sightlines. Incorporating spatial fluctuations in the ionizing mean free path is crucial for matching observations. Accounting for cosmic variance and rare sightlines increases model consistency with observed correlations from 17.5% to 74.1%.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale Lyman-α forest correlations at z=6 can be explained by existing reionization models if rare, highly transmissive sightlines and cosmic variance are properly considered, highlighting the importance of spatial fluctuations in the ionizing mean free path.

title: Disk reflection as the origin of the X-ray polarization of NGC 4151 with IXPE
comment: Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present an X-ray spectro-polarimetric study of the nearby type-1 active galactic nucleus NGC 4151 using two long IXPE observations obtained in 2022 and 2024, supported by simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR spectroscopy. IXPE measures a polarization degree of $\sim 6-7\%$ above 4 keV, with a polarization angle parallel to the radio jet, and a distinct low-energy component with a different angle, indicating at least two polarized components in the $2-8$ keV band. Previous work interpreted the hard X-ray polarization as evidence for a radially extended slab-like corona. Here we test an alternative scenario in which the observed polarization is produced predominantly by relativistic reflection from an accretion disk illuminated by a compact, lamp-post-like corona. Using recently developed models, we fit the IXPE Stokes spectra with a lamp-post plus distant-torus geometry, including partial-covering absorption and an additional soft polarized power-law component. We find that the data require a low coronal height ($h<9\,R_{\rm g}$ at $3σ$) and a relatively large torus opening angle ($>45^\circ$ at 3$σ$), while the disk reflection contributes $\sim 20\%$ of the 2-8 keV flux. The soft polarized component carries only $\sim 1-5\%$ of the flux but has a high polarization degree ($>10\%$) and a polarization angle around $20^\circ$. The same configuration provides acceptable fits to the $0.4-79$ keV XMM-Newton and NuSTAR spectra, demonstrating that disk reprocessing by a compact corona can simultaneously account for both the polarization and broadband spectral properties of NGC 4151.

AI.tldr: This study uses IXPE, XMM-Newton, and NuSTAR data to show that the X-ray polarization in NGC 4151 is best explained by relativistic disk reflection illuminated by a compact corona, rather than a radially extended corona, successfully fitting both polarization and broadband spectra.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of the X-ray polarization observed in the type-1 active galactic nucleus NGC 4151 and to test whether relativistic reflection from an accretion disk illuminated by a compact corona can explain the observed polarization and spectral properties.
AI.method: Performed X-ray spectro-polarimetric analysis using two long IXPE observations from 2022 and 2024, supported by simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR spectroscopy. Applied recently developed theoretical models fitting IXPE Stokes spectra with a lamp-post corona plus distant-torus geometry including partial-covering absorption and an additional soft polarized power-law component.
AI.result: Observed a polarization degree of ~6-7% above 4 keV with distinct polarization angles indicating multiple polarized components. Found that a low coronal height (<9 R_g at 3σ) and large torus opening angle (>45° at 3σ) are required, with disk reflection contributing ~20% of the 2-8 keV flux. The soft polarized component, although weak in flux (~1-5%), shows high polarization degree (>10%) and a distinct polarization angle (~20°). This configuration adequately fits both polarization and broadband spectral data of NGC 4151.
AI.conclusion: Disk reflection from an accretion disk illuminated by a compact lamp-post corona, combined with a large torus opening angle and partial-covering absorption, can explain the observed X-ray polarization and broadband spectral features of NGC 4151, challenging previous interpretations favoring radially extended coronae.

title: $δ$-CDM: A Minimal Deformation of $Λ$CDM with Scalar Field Reconstruction
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures
summary: Recent DESI BAO observations provide intriguing hints that dark energy may be dynamical in nature. To investigate deviations of the dark energy equation of state (EoS) from $w = -1$, we introduce the $δ$-CDM framework, a controlled deformation of $Λ$CDM in which deviations from a cosmological constant are parametrized by a redshift-dependent function $δ(z)$, defined through $w_{\rm de}(z) = -1 + δ(z)$. As an illustrative example, we reconstruct $δ(z)$ using effective scalar field dynamics of thawing type, encompassing both quintessence and phantom regimes within a unified description. Notably, the reconstructed $δ(z)$ is independent of the specific scalar field realization, ensuring theoretical robustness. Using Planck CMB-SPA data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and the Pantheon+ supernova sample within a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis, we find that the $\tilde{w}_0\tilde{w}_a$ parametrization is preferred over this thawing-type realization of deviations from $w = -1$. Overall, the $δ$-CDM framework provides a minimal yet flexible extension of $Λ$CDM, capable of capturing late-time dynamical features of dark energy.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the δ-CDM framework to model dynamical dark energy deviations from w = -1 using a redshift-dependent function δ(z). It reconstructs δ(z) via thawing scalar field dynamics and employs Bayesian analysis on cosmological datasets, finding that traditional w0wa parametrization fits data better, while δ-CDM offers a robust and flexible extension of ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To investigate possible deviations in the dark energy equation of state from the cosmological constant form (w = -1) suggested by recent DESI BAO observations.
AI.method: Introducing the δ-CDM framework that parametrizes deviations via a redshift-dependent function δ(z), reconstructing δ(z) using effective scalar field dynamics of thawing type, and performing Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis with Planck CMB-SPA data, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova samples.
AI.result: The w0wa parametrization is preferred over the thawing-type scalar field realization, and the δ-CDM framework successfully captures late-time dynamical features of dark energy with theoretical robustness independent of specific scalar field models.
AI.conclusion: The δ-CDM framework is a minimal, flexible extension of ΛCDM that effectively models dynamical dark energy deviations, providing insight into potential late-time dynamics indicated by observational data.

title: Relativistic Thermal Emission from Accretion Disks in Kerr-MOG Spacetimes
comment: 16pages, 11 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: In Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity (STVG, also known as MOG), a massive vector field $φ_μ$ generates a repulsive fifth force that endows rotating black holes with a gravitational charge $Q \propto \sqrtα\,M$, modifying the near-horizon geometry through a single deformation parameter $α$. We investigate how this vector-field coupling imprints itself on the thermal continuum emission of geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disks in the Kerr-MOG black hole. By re-deriving the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the Novikov-Thorne radiative flux, the relativistic energy shift, and the null geodesic structure for the Kerr-MOG spacetime, we compute fully relativistic disk spectra across a broad range of spins, inclinations, and fifth-force strengths using a dedicated \textsc{xspec} spectral model (\texttt{kmspec}). We find that the fifth-force charge pushes the ISCO outward, lowers the peak disk temperature, and systematically softens the thermal continuum relative to its Kerr black hole counterpart at the same spin, with the deviation amplified at high observer inclinations. The resulting spectral modification closely mimics a reduction of spin in the pure Kerr black hole framework, indicating that independent spin measurements from, e.g., iron-line reflection spectroscopy are indispensable for disentangling the vector-field contribution. All results recover the standard Kerr black hole predictions when $α= 0$, and the model is validated against independent analytic and numerical benchmarks to machine precision. Application to a 69.6~ks \textit{XMM-Newton} observation of LMC~X-1 yields $α< 0.044$ at 90\% confidence, consistent with the Kerr metric and general relativity.

AI.tldr: This work models how a vector-field-induced fifth force in modified gravity alters accretion disk emission around rotating black holes, creating spectral signatures that resemble lower spin. Using relativistic spectral modeling and X-ray data from LMC X-1, it constrains deviations from Kerr black holes, reinforcing agreement with general relativity.
AI.motivation: To investigate how the repulsive fifth force from a massive vector field in Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity (STVG/MOG) affects the thermal emission properties of accretion disks around rotating black holes.
AI.method: Re-derivation of key orbital and radiative properties (ISCO, Novikov-Thorne flux, energy shifts, null geodesics) in Kerr-MOG spacetime; development of a fully relativistic disk spectral model (kmspec) in xspec; comparison of spectra across varying spins, inclinations, and fifth-force strengths; validation against analytic and numerical benchmarks; application to XMM-Newton observations of LMC X-1.
AI.result: The fifth-force charge increases the ISCO radius, reduces peak disk temperature, and softens the thermal continuum spectrum compared to standard Kerr black holes, particularly at high inclinations. The spectral changes mimic a lower spin in Kerr models, requiring complementary spin measurements to isolate the vector field effects. Observational constraints from LMC X-1 limit the deformation parameter to α < 0.044, consistent with Kerr and general relativity.
AI.conclusion: The presence of a fifth-force charge in Kerr-MOG black holes significantly modifies accretion disk spectra in a way that can be observationally constrained. The model successfully recovers Kerr results when the deformation parameter α is zero, and current X-ray data supports consistency with general relativity, placing upper limits on deviations from Kerr geometry.

title: Bayesian Reconstruction of the Local Universe from 2MRS: Testing the Gravitational Flow with Cosmicflows-4
comment: 21 pages, 7 figures
summary: We present a Bayesian reconstruction of the local density and velocity fields traced by the 2MASS Redshift Survey (2MRS) and test the inferred gravitational flow against independent Cosmicflows-4 (CF4) galaxy-group peculiar velocities. The fiducial reconstruction is the maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) solution of a Zel'dovich-approximation forward model, constrained by the 2MRS redshift-space distribution through an unbinned Poisson point-process likelihood. The model assumes Gaussian initial conditions and includes the 2MRS selection function, the Zone of Avoidance, redshift-space distortions, and a distance-dependent galaxy-bias prescription. Hamiltonian Monte Carlo provides posterior samples and constrained realizations within the same framework. The reconstructed velocity field agrees well with CF4 in object-by-object, density--velocity-correlation, and shell-by-shell reflex-dipole tests. These comparisons are made at the CF4 redshift-space positions and do not require smoothing the observed CF4 velocities to the MAP resolution. We also evolve constrained initial conditions with Gadget-4. The real-space density retains the large-scale Zel'dovich structure while developing additional nonlinear small-scale structure, and the redshift-space distribution develops nonlinear Fingers of God. The results show that the 2MRS field-level reconstruction captures the large-scale gravitational flow of the nearby Universe and provides initial conditions suitable for constrained simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian method to reconstruct local cosmic density and velocity fields from 2MRS data, validating the results against Cosmicflows-4 velocities and simulations, demonstrating successful recovery of large-scale gravitational flows and generation of realistic initial conditions for simulations.
AI.motivation: To reconstruct local density and velocity fields from galaxy survey data to understand gravitational flows in the nearby Universe.
AI.method: Bayesian reconstruction using a Zel'dovich-approximation forward model constrained by 2MRS redshift-space data, incorporating Gaussian initial conditions, selection functions, and galaxy bias, with posterior sampling via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo; followed by evolving constrained initial conditions with Gadget-4 simulations.
AI.result: The reconstructed velocity field matches well with independent Cosmicflows-4 galaxy-group velocities across multiple tests without requiring velocity smoothing; nonlinear small-scale structures emerge in simulations, confirming the reconstruction's accuracy and suitability for constrained simulations.
AI.conclusion: The 2MRS Bayesian field-level reconstruction effectively captures the large-scale gravitational flow in the nearby Universe, providing reliable initial conditions for further constrained cosmological simulations.

title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Space-borne Detectors
comment: 18 pages, 13 figures, 10 tables
summary: Future space-borne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of space-borne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as \textbf{GW-LMC-Space}. Our results show that, for a four-year LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from $0$ to $131$, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to $\sim 0.3\%$. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a one-year observation is expected to lie in the range of $0$--$44$, with a lensing probability of $\sim 0.15\%$ for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). We further show that the overlap of lensed signals is a common feature in space-borne detectors, which can significantly affect both the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimation and event identification. These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future space-borne GW observations.

AI.tldr: This work presents a comprehensive simulation framework for strongly lensed gravitational-wave events in space-borne detectors, predicting up to hundreds of such events with noticeable lensing probabilities and highlighting signal overlap as a critical factor in their detection and analysis.
AI.motivation: Future space-borne gravitational-wave detectors are expected to detect many events, some of which may be strongly lensed, necessitating a framework to simulate these events realistically.
AI.method: Development of a comprehensive simulation framework based on realistic astrophysical models to create mock catalogs of strongly lensed gravitational-wave events for space-borne detectors like LISA and DECIGO.
AI.result: For a four-year LISA mission, the expected number of lensed events ranges from 0 to 131 with lensing probabilities up to ~0.3% for massive black hole binaries; for DECIGO, 0 to 44 events in one year with lensing probabilities ~0.15%. Overlap of lensed signals is common and significantly affects SNR estimation and event identification.
AI.conclusion: Strongly lensed gravitational-wave events are expected in future space-borne detectors with non-negligible probabilities, and signal overlap must be accounted for to ensure accurate analysis of these events.

title: Precise scaling relations for self-interacting bosonic dark matter stars
summary: The structural properties of bosonic dark matter stars are systematically investigated, presenting precise scaling relations for the mass, radius, central density, and the properties of dark matter particles. The dark matter equation of state is derived from a complex scalar field theory with a quartic self-interaction potential $V(φ) = \fracλ{4} |φ|^4$, considering boson masses $m_φ$ ranging from $10^{-9}$ to $10^{3}$ GeV and self-coupling constants $λ$ ranging from $0.01π$ to $100π$. The scaling relation for the maximum mass of bosonic dark matter stars, the corresponding critical radius and critical central density are obtained as \[ M_{\text{max}} = 0.1 \frac{\sqrtλ}{m_φ^2} M_\odot, \qquad R(M_{\text{max}}) = 0.9 \frac{\sqrtλ}{m_φ^2} \ \text{km}, \qquad \varepsilon_{\text{max}} = 2.1 \times 10^5 \frac{m_φ^4}λ \ \mathrm{MeV/fm^3}, \] where $m_φ$ is in GeV, the relations for $R(M_{\text{max}})$ and $\varepsilon_{\text{max}}$ are first put forward. The fitting relative error is less than $4\%$. Based on these scaling relations, we further provide global analytical fits for the stable branch. The relationships between mass and central density as well as radius and central density can be described by a unified function of the form: \[ \tilde{Y} = \frac{A}{\left[1 + \left(5\tilde{\varepsilon}\right)^h\right]^s}, \] where for $Y=M$, $\tilde{M} \equiv M/M_{\text{max}}$, $A=1$, $h=-2$, $s=0.42$; for $Y=R$, $\tilde{R} \equiv R/R(M_{\text{max}})$, $A=1.634$, $h=1$, $s=0.28$; and $\tilde{\varepsilon} \equiv \varepsilon_0/\varepsilon_{\text{max}}$. The fitting relative error is less than $0.1\%$. Furthermore, we find a simple quadratic polynomial mass-radius relation for bosonic dark matter stars.

AI.tldr: This paper develops precise scaling relations and analytical fits describing the mass, radius, and central density of bosonic dark matter stars derived from a scalar field theory with quartic self-interaction, covering a wide range of boson masses and coupling constants, enabling accurate predictions of their structural properties.
AI.motivation: To systematically investigate and precisely characterize the structural properties of bosonic dark matter stars across a broad parameter range, addressing the lack of established scaling relations for their mass, radius, and central density, particularly to improve understanding of bosonic dark matter properties in astrophysical compact objects.
AI.method: The study derives the dark matter equation of state from a complex scalar field theory with a quartic self-interaction potential, systematically exploring a wide parameter space of boson masses and self-coupling constants, and fitting analytical scaling relations to the numerical results.
AI.result: The paper presents new scaling relations for maximum mass, critical radius, and central density with fitting errors under 4%, proposes global analytical fits for the stable branch with fitting errors below 0.1%, and identifies a simple quadratic polynomial mass-radius relation, all providing tools to understand bosonic dark matter stars' structure in terms of boson mass and self-interaction strength.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes precise and novel scaling relations for the maximum mass, radius, and central density of bosonic dark matter stars, along with highly accurate global analytical fits describing stable configurations and a simple quadratic mass-radius relation.

title: Optimising ultra-light dark matter searches with ground-based interferometers
comment: 35 pages, 11 figures
summary: Ultra-light dark matter fields induce nearly monochromatic signals in gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to the Standard Model. Their spectral morphology exhibits features caused by sidereal modulation that, for frequencies below $\sim 30~$Hz, enable discrimination between spin-1 and spin-2 ultra-light dark matter signals, provided sufficient signal-to-noise ratio. In the context of LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA search techniques, we show that incorporating these spectral features can improve current excess-power constraints at low frequencies by up to $\sim36\%$. Additionally, we propose an optimised implementation of the cross-correlation statistics within the Band-Sampled-Data framework, enhancing the sensitivity of cross-correlation searches across nearly the entire frequency range, reaching up to $\sim42\%$ at low frequencies and $\sim35\%$ at high frequencies.

AI.tldr: This paper improves the detection of ultra-light dark matter via gravitational-wave detectors by leveraging spectral features from sidereal modulation and optimizing cross-correlation methods, boosting sensitivity by up to ~42% across frequency ranges.
AI.motivation: To improve the detection and discrimination of ultra-light dark matter signals in gravitational-wave data by exploiting unique spectral features induced by their coupling to the Standard Model, particularly at low frequencies.
AI.method: Analysis of sidereal modulation effects on spectral morphology of ultra-light dark matter signals; incorporation of these features into LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA search techniques; development of an optimized cross-correlation statistic implementation within the Band-Sampled-Data framework.
AI.result: Demonstrated that incorporating spectral features improves excess-power constraints at low frequencies by up to ~36%; optimized cross-correlation statistics enhance search sensitivity by ~42% at low frequencies and ~35% at high frequencies.
AI.conclusion: Utilizing sidereal modulation features and optimized cross-correlation methods significantly enhances the sensitivity and discrimination capability of gravitational-wave detectors for ultra-light dark matter signals, advancing the effectiveness of current search strategies.

title: Modifying $Λ$CDM dynamics via out-of-equilibrium axions: reconciling SH0ES and DESI $H_0$ values
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures
summary: We investigate late-Universe dynamics in which the dark matter component is described by axion particles. The proposed framework departs from the standard $Λ$CDM paradigm due to a small fraction of axions driving the system away from thermal equilibrium. We analyze the evolution of the axion energy density using both a kinetic and a classical field approach, yielding an identical macroscopic evolution equation for the dark matter density. The resulting scenario modifies $Λ$CDM dynamics in the late Universe (specifically at $z \lesssim 1$), while asymptotically recovering the standard baseline at earlier cosmic epochs. We compare the theoretical predictions of our formulation against a comprehensive suite of late-Universe datasets. Our statistical analysis reveals that when the SH0ES local calibration is included, the collisional axion model becomes significantly favored over $Λ$CDM, yielding a best-fit Hubble constant of $H_0 \simeq 73~{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. Ultimately, this cosmological scenario successfully accommodates local distance-ladder measurements while maintaining excellent agreement with Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the DESI Collaboration.

AI.tldr: Introducing a small fraction of axion dark matter out of thermal equilibrium modifies late-Universe dynamics, resolving the Hubble tension and fitting both local and BAO data better than ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To explore modifications to late-Universe dynamics by introducing an axion dark matter component that deviates from thermal equilibrium, aiming to address tensions in cosmological observations such as the Hubble constant discrepancy.
AI.method: Analyzed axion energy density evolution using both kinetic theory and classical field approaches, deriving a unified macroscopic evolution equation for dark matter; performed statistical comparison of model predictions against late-Universe observational datasets including SH0ES local calibration and DESI BAO data.
AI.result: The collisional axion model modifies late-time cosmic dynamics (z <~ 1) while reverting to standard ΛCDM at earlier epochs; it is significantly favored over ΛCDM when including SH0ES data, yielding a higher best-fit Hubble constant (H0 ≈ 73 km/s/Mpc) and maintaining consistency with BAO measurements.
AI.conclusion: A small axion dark matter fraction driving the system away from thermal equilibrium provides a viable late-Universe cosmological scenario that alleviates the H0 tension while preserving concordance with large-scale structure data, suggesting potential advantages over the standard ΛCDM model.

title: Spectral distortion anisotropies from photon to dark photon conversions
comment: 37 pages, 14 figures, to be submitted to JCAP, comments welcome!
summary: Dark photons are a gauge boson of a hypothetical dark sector, representing one of the most-studied minimal extensions of the Standard Model, with wide-ranging theoretical and observational implications. Here, we consider scenarios in which an initially unpopulated dark photon sector is populated via resonant photon to dark photon conversions. This process leads to observable spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background (CMB), that can be used to constrain these models. We extend previous spectral distortion studies of the monopole spectrum to anisotropic spectral distortions, using the newly developed Frequency Hierarchy (FH) framework of CosmoTherm. We illustrate the physics by presenting detailed computations of the photon transfer functions and distortion cross power spectra throughout the dark photon parameter space. We find that the dark photon mass explicitly controls the shape (i.e., multipole-dependence) of the signal power spectra, while the overall amplitude of the signal is determined by the kinetic mixing parameter of the model. Using these results, we place complementary limits on the minimal dark photon model using data from Planck, finding that the constraints are only marginally weaker than those obtained with COBE/FIRAS data for the average (monopole) distortion. In addition, we compute the corrections to the standard temperature field, arguing that conversions at redshifts larger than $2\times 10^6$ may add iso-curvature type perturbations, which could lead to novel constraints in regimes where distortion anisotropies thermalize.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how resonant conversions between photons and dark photons affect anisotropic spectral distortions in the CMB, using a new computational framework to derive constraints comparable to existing monopole analyses and highlighting potential new cosmological signatures.
AI.motivation: To explore the effects of resonant photon to dark photon conversions in an initially unpopulated dark photon sector and their observable consequences on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions, particularly anisotropic spectral distortions.
AI.method: Extension of previous spectral distortion studies from monopole to anisotropic distortions using the Frequency Hierarchy (FH) framework of CosmoTherm; detailed computations of photon transfer functions and distortion cross power spectra across the dark photon parameter space.
AI.result: Discovery that the dark photon mass controls the shape of the signal power spectra's multipole dependence, while the kinetic mixing parameter determines the overall amplitude; constraints on the minimal dark photon model from Planck data closely rival those from COBE/FIRAS data; identification of potential iso-curvature perturbations from high-redshift conversions that may lead to new constraints.
AI.conclusion: Anisotropic spectral distortions provide complementary and nearly competitive constraints on dark photon models compared to monopole studies, with the dark photon mass and kinetic mixing parameter influencing distinct features of the signal; moreover, early-universe conversions may induce novel iso-curvature perturbations, opening new avenues for constraining the dark photon parameter space.

title: Fast Radio Bursts produced during collapse of macroscopic X-mode in magnetized pair plasma
comment: videos are in the Ancillary Folder ./anc
summary: We demonstrate that in highly magnetized pair plasma nonlinear long-wavelength X-modes experience wave collapse/breaking, whereby the wave undergoes severe spatial steepening, driven by nonlinear modifications of the refractive index and strong ponderomotive forces. The collapse/wave breaking occurs in a narrow parameter regime, when the fluctuating part of the magnetic field exceed the guide field, and plasma magnetization is close to the current starvation regime. This regime is naturally achieved in highly magnetized neutron stars, magnetars. Breaking occurs on the time scale of a fraction of the dynamic time scale, and quickly generates high-k modes. The initial EM energy, spread over large spatial scales, is squeezed into these highly localized, short-wavelength (yet macroscopic) singular pulses. The corresponding electromagnetic ``foam'' spectrum is red, $E_k \propto k^{-2}$, while the particles' spectrum is exceptionally hard, $f(γ) \propto γ^0$ The wave collapse produces short bright EM pulses - astrophysical Fast Radio Bursts. The highest energy particles may produce short high energy bursts.

AI.tldr: Nonlinear wave collapse in magnetar-like pair plasma creates localized intense EM pulses and hard particle spectra, offering a mechanism for Fast Radio Bursts and high-energy bursts.
AI.motivation: To understand the nonlinear wave dynamics in highly magnetized pair plasma relevant to astrophysical environments such as magnetars.
AI.method: Analyzing nonlinear long-wavelength X-mode wave behavior under strong magnetization, focusing on wave collapse and breaking due to nonlinear refractive index modifications and ponderomotive forces.
AI.result: Identification of a narrow regime where wave collapse occurs when magnetic field fluctuations exceed the guide field near current starvation conditions, leading to rapid generation of high-k modes and formation of localized, short-wavelength electromagnetic pulses with a red foam spectrum and hard particle energy spectrum.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear wave collapse in highly magnetized pair plasma can produce bright, short electromagnetic pulses that can explain astrophysical phenomena like Fast Radio Bursts and associated high-energy particle bursts.

title: Pantheon+ supernovae corrected for progenitor age indicate the universe is decelerating
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables; to appear as a Letter in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: We examine the impact of progenitor age-dependent luminosity evolution of Type Ia supernovae on a cosmographic measurement of the deceleration parameter $q_0$. Our recent redshift tomographic analysis showed that locally $q_0$ has a strong dipole anisotropy aligned approximately with the bulk flow, and only a small monopole component remains at distances exceeding a few hundred Mpc. Applying redshift-dependent corrections for progenitor age to the Pantheon+ catalogue, we find that this shifts the monopole component of $q_0$ to positive values (i.e. deceleration), while leaving the local dipole component essentially unchanged.

AI.tldr: Correcting Type Ia supernova luminosities for progenitor age shifts the cosmic deceleration parameter’s monopole component to positive values, implying deceleration, but leaves the local anisotropic dipole structure unchanged.
AI.motivation: To investigate how progenitor age-dependent luminosity evolution of Type Ia supernovae affects cosmographic measurements, particularly the deceleration parameter q0.
AI.method: Applied redshift-dependent corrections accounting for progenitor age to the Pantheon+ supernovae catalogue and performed a redshift tomographic analysis to measure q0's monopole and dipole components.
AI.result: Found that correcting for progenitor age shifts q0's monopole component towards positive values (indicating deceleration) at large distances, while the local dipole anisotropy remains largely unaffected.
AI.conclusion: Progenitor age-dependent luminosity evolution impacts the inferred large-scale monopole component of cosmic deceleration but does not explain the local anisotropic dipole observed in q0 measurements.

title: A thousand looks at X Persei: X-ray spectroscopy at high time resolution
summary: X Persei is a classical Be/X-ray binary composed of an O9.5III-B0V Be-type star and a neutron star (NS). The NS exhibits coherent pulsations with a spin period of ~837 s, orbiting the Be star with a ~250 d period. X Persei is notable for its exceptionally hard X-ray emission extending beyond 100 keV. Due to the mild eccentricity of the orbit, ~0.11, the orbital separation varies between roughly 35 R_star at periastron and 44 R_star at apastron. In this work, we analyze five targeted observations obtained with the XMM-Newton and Chandra observatories taken over a 10-year time span, with the aim of investigating the structure and variability of the circumstellar disk surrounding the Be star, in particular the presence of over-dense areas known as clumps. We performed spectral and timing analyses, including average and NS spin-resolved spectroscopy for three of the observations, producing individual spectra at intervals as short as 210 s, corresponding to different epochs of the NS spin, resulting in approximately 1200 spectra. This detailed analysis aimed at resolving emission-line features otherwise diluted in averaged spectra and the evolution of continuum components along the NS spin. The observed spectra are accurately modeled by a two-component continuum comprising a high-temperature blackbody and a power-law component. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals transient Fe K alpha emission linked to clumps in the circumstellar disk during high-density epochs, with an 8-9% prevalence. Dips in the X-ray light curve are tied to clump passages. The disk-density modeling, based solely on X-ray data, suggests a compact and dense disk, with a radial density exponent alpha of 2.4-3.3, and a high inner disk density, rho_0 ~ (6-20) x 10^-10 g cm^-3, in agreement with previous studies conducted in the optical and infrared bands.

AI.tldr: This study used decade-spanning XMM-Newton and Chandra data to perform detailed spin-resolved spectroscopy of the X Persei system, revealing dense clumps in the Be star's circumstellar disk that modulate X-ray emission and confirming a compact, dense disk structure consistent with previous optical and infrared observations.
AI.motivation: To investigate the structure and variability of the circumstellar disk around the Be star in the X Persei system, particularly focusing on the presence and effects of over-dense clumps.
AI.method: Analyzed five observations from XMM-Newton and Chandra over 10 years, performing spectral and timing analyses, including average and neutron star spin-resolved spectroscopy producing about 1200 individual spectra at intervals as short as 210 s to resolve emission-line features and continuum evolution along the NS spin.
AI.result: Identified a two-component continuum (high-temperature blackbody and power-law), transient Fe K alpha emission linked to disk clumps, and X-ray light curve dips associated with clump passages. Disk density modeling indicates a compact, dense disk with radial density exponent 2.4-3.3 and inner density ~6-20 x 10^-10 g cm^-3, consistent with previous optical and IR studies.
AI.conclusion: The detailed X-ray spectral and timing analyses confirm the presence of dense clumps in the Be star's circumstellar disk, which influence X-ray emission features and variability. The density profile derived from X-rays corroborates earlier multiwavelength findings, advancing understanding of Be/X-ray binary disk structure and dynamics.

title: Stochastic constant-roll inflation beyond the hilltop with the spectral method
comment: 40 pages, 10 figures, 1 table
summary: Stochastic inflation can be used to study large inflationary perturbations. This paper presents such a study for a quadratic hilltop potential, corresponding to constant-roll inflation. I solve the perturbation distribution using the spectral method, with detailed solutions of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Fokker-Planck operator. Contrary to previous studies of stochastic constant-roll inflation, the solution allows trajectories that cross the hilltop and get stuck near a reflecting boundary on the other side, tunneling out slowly in a way dictated by the lowest eigensolution. Despite their rarity, these trajectories turn out to dominate the mean first-passage time. For this reason, I argue the mean does not properly describe the inflationary background. Using the median instead, I compute the distribution of the coarse-grained $ΔN$ distribution and show that its well-known exponential tail first flattens out and then forms a peak near a maximal $ΔN$ value. I argue similar intricacies arise in primordial black hole models.

AI.tldr: Using spectral methods, the paper analyzes stochastic constant-roll inflation with a quadratic hilltop potential, finding rare boundary-crossing trajectories dominate average behavior, invalidating the mean as a descriptor and highlighting the median's relevance. This influences the ΔN distribution shape and informs primordial black hole model understanding.
AI.motivation: To study large inflationary perturbations in a quadratic hilltop potential corresponding to constant-roll inflation using stochastic inflation methods.
AI.method: The perturbation distribution is solved using the spectral method by detailed analysis of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Fokker-Planck operator.
AI.result: The solution reveals the existence of rare trajectories crossing the hilltop and getting stuck near a reflecting boundary, which dominate the mean first-passage time. The mean is thus an inadequate descriptor of the inflationary background; using the median leads to a distribution of coarse-grained ΔN with a characteristic exponential tail that flattens and peaks near a maximal value. Similar effects are expected in primordial black hole models.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that the mean first-passage time is dominated by rare trajectories, making the median a more appropriate statistic to describe the inflationary background under stochastic constant-roll inflation. This provides new insights into the perturbation distribution and has implications for primordial black hole formation scenarios.

title: Modelling Galactic neutrino emission: contributions from massive star clusters and interstellar cosmic rays
comment: 33 pages, 14 figures, submitted to JCAP
summary: The recent detection of Galactic neutrinos by the IceCube Observatory constitutes a remarkable achievement for neutrino astrophysics.
